item.title: Not everything that sounds plausible works: Testing ideas to win support for carbon pricing
item.description: What makes people support a carbon price? To find out, 108 researchers, led by a research team at the University of Innsbruck, Austria, tested 55 different ideas at the same time, from information campaigns to reflection tasks. On average, there was a small but statistically significant positive effect. Individually, the effect was detectable for only 11 of the 55 ideas. One of the strongest effects came from writing a letter to a fictional person of a future generation. The results were recently published in the journal Nature Human Behaviour. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Moment dog and owner get swept up by king tide on Oregon beach – video
item.description: Cannon Beach police department in Oregon posted footage of a man narrowly escaping being swept away by the tide as he walked his dog on the beach on Tuesday. Both made it back to dry land reportedly uninjured. The police said the man had earlier been issued a citation for driving on another beach and had been warned to stay away from the ocean as a 'king tide' was expected. 'King tides', which is not a scientific term, are exceptionally high tides that typically occur during a new or full moon and when the moon is at its perigee. Rising sea levels, combined with El Niño and 'king tides' are… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: New EU Bureaucracy Index: EU law has more than doubled since 2010
item.description: The new EU Bureaucracy Index measures the volume of EU law in force, and it shows a record high: At the end of 2025, the EU regulations and directives in force comprised around 47,600 standard pages, 118% more than in 2010. The volume of EU law has thus more than doubled in 15 years, and it continued to grow in 2025. The main drivers are sanctions regulations and new sets of rules in environmental, consumer and health law. Fuente: Phys.org.
